content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to learn instance-wise segmentation via a box-driven Teacher model. The teacher-student pipeline is linked via the EMA mode. For the student model, the noise reduce mask supervision is introduced. Surely the overall pipeline is good, with necessary experimental comparisons.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1) The main contribution of this paper is Noise-reduced Mask Affinity Loss, while this loss it quite similar with existing BoxInst which also rely on the local relation among neighboring pixels. 
2) The experimental results show the effectiveness with SOTA performance on COCO.

Weakness:
1) The detail of Noise-reduced Mask Affinity Loss is quite coarse which is hard to understand. In Eq3, it is equal to a mean pooling? Eq5 has a same part in the numerator with denominator, what does it mean?  p_i and p_j are not defined.
2) As the results shown in Tab 2, the achieved SOTA performance is powered by the strong backbone Swin-FPN, rather than the proposed method. For example, with R101 backbone, the proposed method is worse than SOTA methods.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1) The paper writing and organization is good, which is clear enough for understanding. 
2) The writing quality and experimental evaluation is good.
3) Novelty is weak, since the key motivation is very similar with BoxInst. If the details of Noise-reduced Mask Affinity Loss are provided, the Reproducibility is ok.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, this is a good paper with a teacher-student pipeline that using denoising loss. Based on the strengths and the weakness, currently, the reviewer suggests a positive rating to this paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper aims to train a high-performance instance segmentation model in a weakly-supervised setting, i.e., with only bounding box annotations. Based on the state-of-the-art box-supervised method BoxInst, the paper further improves it and proposes BoxTeacher, a stronger framework that leverages high-quality predicted masks as pseudo labels. Specifically, BoxTeacher adopts a teacher-student scheme and uses a mask-aware confidence score to estimate the quality of the predicted masks. The paper proposes a modified mask loss which is weighted by the mask-aware confidence score, and a modified affinity loss in BoxInst with locally refined pixel probabilities. State-of-the-art performance is achieved on COCO and Cityscapes datasets in the box-supervised setting.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strengthes
- Box-supervised instance segmentation is a significant problem that has attracted much attention recently. The paper sets new state-of-the-art results in this problem and pushes the limit of label-efficient instance segmentation.
- The motivation is clear. Leveraging the high-quality pseudo labels to improve label efficiency and combining it with the state-of-the-art box-supervised method, i.e., BoxInst, is a straightforward solution.
- Extensive experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods in BoxTeacher and how each component works.

# Weaknesses
- The novelty is not that significant. The paper combines and applies several widely used techniques, e.g.,mask-aware confidence and affinity loss and improves the performance of box-supervised instance segmentation.
- It seems that the proposed framework can also leverage unlabeled data without special modifications, which becomes a weakly semi-supervised learning framework. Did you try that? For example, adding COCO-unlabeled to the training. I think this is very interesting and will make the paper stronger.
- Some existing work in weakly semi-supervised methods also explore combining self-training with weakly-supervised instance segmentation, e.g., [a]. More discussion and comparison are needed.
- In the paragraph Noise-reduced Mask Affinity Loss, BoxInst could be mentioned here, as it also uses the affinity loss as pixel-wise supervision.
- In Eq(2), L_pixel is not defined.

[a] Point-Teaching: Weakly Semi-Supervised Object Detection with Point Annotations
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Good clarity, borderline novelty and quality.
content.summary_of_the_review: I think this is a solid work that pushes the development of label-efficient instance segmentation. But my main concern is on the novelty of the method, which is a little bit weak at this stage. More applications will improve the quality of the paper. At this stage, it's a borderline paper to me.

content.summary_of_the_paper: To improve the performance of instance segmentation with only box annotations, this paper attempts to build higher-quality pseudo labels based on results from BoxInst. A Mask-aware Confidence Score is used to average the probability score of the positive masks inside the ground-truth boxes so that matching pseudo-instance masks to ground-truth bounding boxes can be more accurate. Also, mask affinity loss is utilized to lower the impact of noisy pixels further. Experiments on COCO and Cityscapes show performance improvements compared to box-based methods without self-training modules.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
+ The paper is well-written with good-quality figures. For example, Fig.2 is very helpful in understanding the main idea of this paper.
+ The authors build this paper with solid motivation and observation. The instance results of BoxInsts are sometimes more accurately than ground truth. However, simple self-training with the pseudo labels won't help.
+ According to the ablation experiments on COCO, the proposed strategies effectively improve self-training efficiency.

Cons:
- The main concern of this paper is about novelty. First, the weakly-supervised learning / self-training framework follows the previous work, such as FixMatch and DiscoBox. The pseudo labels of the weakly-supervised learning come from BoxInst. The main contribution is the design of the Mask-aware Confidence Score and the mask affinity loss to get better pseudo labels and reduce noise. However, these two terms are not new. The Mask-aware Confidence Score is the average of positive masks inside the ground-truth boxes. It is a widely used strategy in category losses for object detection and instance segmentation, such as in FCOS and SOLO. The Noise-reduced Mask Affinity Loss is also commonly used for noisy labels, e.g., as Multiple instance learning (MIL) in DiscoBox. In this way, the novelty of this paper is limited.
- As this method is trained with a Mask-aware Confidence Score, it is fairer to compare with the naive self-training, which matches ground truth by this score. So we can know if using a new score and getting pseudo lables will be good enough.
- As in Table 2,  it looks like DiscoBox with R-101 can achieve very similar performance compared to this method. So the improvement over the state-of-the-art is minor.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is a high-quality paper in terms of writing and clarity.  The novelty of this paper is limited. And I believe it won't be difficult to reproduce the experiment.
content.summary_of_the_review: This is a well-written paper with promising results compared to its own baseline. However, as the content of this paper doesn't sound very novel to me, at the current stage I think it's below the acceptance threshold.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to take advantage of high-quality pseudo masks produced by box supervision by using a teacher model and a student model. Besides, the authors utilize mask-aware confidence scores to estimate the quality of masks. The student is normally optimized with the ground-truth boxes and pseudo masks through box-based loss and noise-aware pseudo mask loss.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper is clear and well-written.
2. The ablation study is enough to show the effectiveness of each module.

Weaknesses:
1. The novelty is limited. The teacher-student model is already explored by previous methods[1,2]. And the similar strategy (confidence scores) is already proposed in work[1]. Please discuss the differences from the works[1,2].
2. The authors are encouraged to perform more experiments on various datasets, e.g., Pascal VOC[3]. However, they only conduct experiments on the CoCo dataset.
3. It is suggested to introduce more box-supervised weakly supervised instance segmentation methods in the related work section.


[1] Yang W, Zhang T, Yu X, et al. Uncertainty guided collaborative training for weakly supervised temporal action detection[C]//Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2021: 53-63.

[2] Laine S, Aila T. Temporal ensembling for semi-supervised learning[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:1610.02242, 2016.

[3] Everingham M, Van Gool L, Williams C K I, et al. The pascal visual object classes (voc) challenge[J]. International journal of computer vision, 2010, 88(2): 303-338.

content.summary_of_the_review: The novelty is weak, and the experiments only with the CoCo dataset are not enough to show the superiority of the proposed method.

content.title: BoxTeacher: Exploring High-Quality Pseudo Labels for Weakly Supervised Instance Segmentation
content.TL;DR: This paper presents an end-to-end training framework named BoxTeacher to boost the performance of weakly supervised instance segmentation with high-quality pseudo labels.
content.abstract: Labeling objects with pixel-wise segmentation requires a huge amount of human labor compared to bounding boxes. Most existing methods for weakly supervised instance segmentation focus on designing heuristic losses with priors from bounding boxes. While we find that box-supervised methods can produce some fine segmentation masks and we wonder whether the detectors could learn from these fine masks while ignoring low-quality masks. To answer this question, we present BoxTeacher, an efficient and end-to-end training framework for high-performance weakly supervised instance segmentation, which leverages a sophisticated teacher to generate high-quality masks as pseudo labels. Considering the massive noisy masks hurt the training, we present a mask-aware confidence score to estimate the quality of pseudo masks and propose the noise-aware pixel loss and noise-reduced affinity loss to adaptively optimize the student with pseudo masks. Extensive experiments can demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed BoxTeacher. Without bells and whistles, BoxTeacher remarkably achieves $34.4$ mask AP and $35.4$ mask AP with ResNet-50 and ResNet-101 respectively on the challenging MS-COCO dataset, which outperforms the previous state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin. The code and models will be available later.
